Printed switch-matrix drive column 8, return row 1. The switch-locations parts list marks this position with an unnumbered Sol./Switch entry and the ** footnote 'Optotransistor on Backbox Interconnect Bd'; the physical cabinet flipper button (SW-10A-48 left / SW-1010A-13 right) has no matrix address of its own and switches coil power directly through the hardware relay/fuse circuit, with no independent CPU coil drive. The factory Power Wiring Diagram (PDF 106/printed 96) shows the input LED of 2U3 on a resistor-fed sensing branch between the flipper supply and the switched lower-coil return (BLU-VIO right), in parallel with the coil load. Its output transistor is optically isolated on the matrix side, allowing the CPU to sense lower-flipper activation here. The lower-coil return runs directly via 2P8/2J8 to the cabinet button; the linked upper-right BLK-YEL return is not monitored by 2U3. The normally-open button removes the return path at rest, so the opto is off and the matrix contact rests open. Pinned PinMAME declares FLIP_SWNO(58,57) (58=left, 57=right). A consumer cannot drive this address: with keyboard handling off (the LibPinMAME default, and the retained script sets HandleKeyboard=0) core_updateSw rewrites it on every update from PinMAME's flipper column, public 82 (the right cabinet button, CORE_SWLRFLIPBUTBIT). The ROM therefore reads the button state exactly as the host writes it there, 1 while the button is pressed, which is what the retained script's S11.VBS flipper keys produce. The retained script also writes Controller.Switch(57) directly from the flipper key (script.vbs lines 1613/1615 and 1629/1631); those writes are overwritten on the next update and have no effect, a defect of the table rather than a fact about the machine.

inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Lower Right End-of-Stroke (81)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT = 0x01, published at 81 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS (implied by FLIP_SOL), and FLIP_SWNO(58,57) sets neither, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8. S11.VBS names this address swURFlip; its vpmKeyDown/vpmKeyUp write it from a staged right-flipper key only while vpmFlips.FlipperSolNumber(3) is non-zero, which core.vbs makes the default (sURFlipper = 34) unless the table calls NoUpperRightFlipper, directly or through core.vbs's cvpmFlips2.Init, which vpmInit runs and which calls it when the table defines cSingleRFlip as a number other than True. The constant does not follow the PinMAME column, and the ROM cannot read the address on this machine, so any such write has no effect.

inputs.label: Lower Right Flipper Button (PinMAME Flipper Column)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPBUTBIT = 0x02, published at 82 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. This is the lower right cabinet flipper button as the ROM receives it. The driver declares FLIP_SWNO(58,57) with no FLIP_SOL, so with keyboard handling off (the LibPinMAME default) core_updateSw reads this bit as the host wrote it and, on every update, copies it into matrix switch 57 through core_setSw and fabricates the synthetic 45/46 flipper outputs from it while the switched-solenoid enable is on. Drive this address, not 57: a host write to 57 is overwritten on the next update. The retained known-working script drives it: Table1_KeyDown/Table1_KeyUp hand the right flipper key to KeyDownHandler/KeyUpHandler, which core.vbs routes to S11.VBS vpmKeyDown/vpmKeyUp, and those set Controller.Switch(swLRFlip) with swLRFlip = 82 (excerpt vpm-script-library-flippers). The physical counterpart is the right cabinet flipper button, which directly switches coil power through the hardware circuit with no independent CPU coil drive. Lower-flipper activation is sensed at matrix 57 by the optically isolated output transistor of 2U3; its input LED is on a resistor-fed branch between the flipper supply and switched lower-coil return (BLU-VIO), in parallel with the coil load. The lower-coil return runs directly via 2P8/2J8 to the button. The linked upper-right BLK-YEL return is not monitored by 2U3. The factory Power Wiring Diagram (PDF 106/printed 96) draws each cabinet button return contact open at rest, removing the return path and leaving the opto off, establishing normally_closed=false independently of public host-input levels.

mechanisms.behavior: A single motor (Wheels Drive Assembly, p/n D-13199) drives a shaft/pinion/gear train (72T/84T/115T gears) turning three playfield discs (LeftWheel, MiddleWheel, RightWheel) simultaneously through solenoid 41. The retained script spins the middle disc opposite sense (+50) from the two outer discs (-50) and coasts the assembly down (SpinnerStep decays by 0.05/tick) rather than stopping instantly when the solenoid de-energizes. The Wheels Drive Assembly parts list lists no switch, opto, or sensor part of any kind, and no Controller.Switch call anywhere in the retained script is associated with any of the three discs or their cvpmTurntable collision helpers -- both independent sources agree this is a pure motor-driven obstacle with no position or ball-pass feedback.
mechanisms.label: Three motorized spinning discs

mechanisms.behavior: Solenoid 6 raps a knocker coil mounted in the backbox to give an audible award/replay signal; no switch is associated with it.
mechanisms.label: Backbox knocker

mechanisms.behavior: A blower motor mounted atop the backbox (driven via the Sound Overlay Solenoid Board and a Triac board, p/n 14-7956) with no associated switch. The retained script only toggles a backglass glow cue (FlSol38) and starts/stops a 'Topper_Fan' sound effect; no fan mesh exists anywhere in the retained table's extraction.
mechanisms.label: Cabinet blower fan

mechanisms.behavior: A ball draining from the playfield lands in the outhole (switch 10) and is kicked into the trough proper (solenoid 1, Outhole Kicker); up to three balls queue at trough positions 1-3 (switches 11-13); solenoid 2 (Shooter Lane Feeder) ejects the lead ball into the shooter lane through the BallRelease kicker. The retained script manages all four switches through its cvpmBallStack helper (bsTrough.InitSw 10,11,12,13) with no individual per-position trigger objects.
mechanisms.label: Four-position ball trough and outhole

mechanisms.behavior: A ball entering the right cellar opening (switch 19, kCellarRight) or left cellar opening (switch 20, kCellarLeft) travels through a below-playfield subway; solenoid 14 (Cellar Kickback) ejects it back to the playfield through the left cellar exit (kCellarLeft, exit speed/angle 157/16 per the retained script's cvpmTrough helper).
mechanisms.label: Left/right cellar subway

mechanisms.behavior: A locking kickback assembly (p/n B-13269) holds up to three balls in a row along the left playfield edge, sensed by switches 22 (lower), 23 (middle), and 24 (upper). Solenoid 4 (Left Locking Kickback) releases the chain by firing Kicker3, then (on Kicker3's own hit event) Kicker2, then Kicker1 in sequence, walking a ball down from the top position to the exit.
mechanisms.label: Three-position left ball lock

mechanisms.behavior: A ball resting on switch 43 (Top Right Eject, the saucer's own named kicker object) is kicked back to the playfield by solenoid 5 (Top Eject) through the retained script's cvpmBallStack saucer helper.
mechanisms.label: Top-right saucer/eject hole

mechanisms.behavior: Solenoid 3 (Right Ramp Lifter) raises the right ramp entry into its 'up' geometry (RightRampUp visible and collidable, RightRampDown hidden) and solenoid 22 (Right Ramp Down, a 'special' solenoid) reverses it; the retained script tracks which geometry is active directly via Controller.Switch(42), matching switch 42's real printed part (5647-12001-00) even though no separate VPX trigger object senses it. Solenoid 13 (Diverter) independently rotates a playfield diverter (25deg/0deg) that steers ball flow near the ramp entrance.
mechanisms.label: Right ramp lifter/diverter

mechanisms.behavior: A single drop target (switch 26, opto-sensed via the 1-Bank Opto Board C-13311) and a 3-bank drop target group (switches 27-29, opto-sensed via the 3-Bank Opto Board C-13205-1) are reset by solenoids 8 and 7 respectively. The retained script's dtT/dtL drop-target helper objects fire Hit(1)/Hit(2)/Hit(3) as each bank target falls.
mechanisms.label: Single and 3-bank opto drop targets

mechanisms.behavior: Two clusters of three jet bumpers each: an upper cluster near the top of the playfield (switches 49-51, solenoids 17/19/21) and a lower cluster nearer the cellar (switches 52-54, solenoids 9/15/10). Each bumper's coil and switch belong to one assembly. The Playfield Parts table identifies red B-9414-3 and yellow B-9414-2 jet assemblies, both with B-9415-1 coil/bracket assemblies.
mechanisms.label: Six-bumper jet nest (two triangular clusters)

mechanisms.behavior: Two slingshot kickers (BL/BR Kicker, each a paired kicker-actuating switch assembly per the switch-locations *** footnote) sensed at switches 55/56 and fired by solenoids 18/20. The retained script's LeftSlingShot_Slingshot/RightSlingShot_Slingshot handlers play a multi-frame flip-book animation on each kick.
mechanisms.label: Bottom-left and bottom-right slingshot kickers

mechanisms.behavior: Three physical flipper assemblies (Lower Left C-11626-L-3, Lower Right C-11626-R-3, Upper Right C-11626-R-3; no upper-left flipper exists). Pinned PinMAME declares FLIP_SWNO(58,57) with no FLIP_SOL bit: the cabinet flipper buttons (SW-10A-48 left, SW-1010A-13 right) fire their coils directly through a relay/fuse circuit with no independent CPU coil drive (no public solenoid address corresponds to a real driver-board output). Backbox Interconnect Board optocouplers 2U2/2U3 sense lower-flipper activation: their input LEDs are on resistor-fed branches from the flipper supply to the switched lower-coil returns (BLU-GRY left, BLU-VIO right), in parallel with the coil loads; their optically isolated output transistors report to the CPU at matrix 58 (left) and 57 (right) for 'Flipper Lane Change'. The lower-coil returns run directly via 2P8/2J8 to the cabinet buttons; the linked upper-right BLK-YEL return is not monitored by 2U3. The normally-open buttons remove the return paths at rest, leaving the optos off. In PinMAME the button state enters at public 82 (right) and 84 (left), which core_updateSw copies into 57/58 and into the synthetic outputs 45-48; a consumer drives 82/84, never 57/58. The retained script's SolRFlipper handler rotates both RightFlipper (lower) and RightFlipper1 (upper) together. The Power Wiring Diagram (printed 96) shows two separate right coils and EOS switches wired to the same right cabinet button.

physical.notes: Printed Solenoid Table entry 11 (Controlled). Retained script callback: SolUpperGI. Pinned PinMAME's whirl_ MACHINE_INIT block names this address 'Upper Playfield GI output' (CORE_MODOUT_BULB_44_6_3V_AC_REV), confirmed by the manual's own GI relay board page (printed 53) and the retained script's SolUpperGI handler. The power schematic (printed 96) routes VIO / WHT-VIO via 2J9-5/1 to this relay. The factory D13356 elevation and original silkscreened board corroborate five rear-panel GI positions, LMP6-LMP10; an actual traced purple/white-purple inline connection and successful repair establish their parallel membership in this branch. Original-stock photographs expose ten upper-playfield bayonets: two deep left, three left-curve, three rear-right and two inner-right. Actual VIO/WHT-VIO feeds, local links, factory routing, regional voltage observations and independently authored 4K switched socket depictions reconcile this inventory. Quantity 15 includes those ten and five D13356 GI lamps. The ten playfield positions use exact Bigus bulb meshes cross-checked against 4K socket mouths and independently read stock wood apertures. The five upright rear-panel GI bulbs are separately projected onto their own corroborated front plastic plane, with factory/physical PCB registration and independent assembled/mounted checks; this does not assert actual PCB depth or filament height. Both three-bank bayonets belong to lower 16: Bigus Light81's upper membership is a renderer defect. The left white curve's fourth opening carries a wire-gate leg and is not another lamp. Value 1 on this public address commands GI darkness and 0 commands light in SolUpperGI; this is a relay command, not direct lamp intensity.

Printed Solenoid Table entry 16 (Controlled). Retained script callback: SolLowerGI. Pinned PinMAME's whirl_ MACHINE_INIT block names this address 'Backbox and Lower playfield GI output'. The manual's own GI relay board page (printed 53) confirms this single address energizes TWO physically separate relays simultaneously: the playfield-side C-11902-1 board (lower playfield GI) and the separate backbox C-11998-1 board (backbox/backglass GI). The retained script's SolLowerGI handler drives both the LowerGI light collection (one member, Light1) and the near-full-table Flasher4 overlay together. That single light and overlay simplify the actual inventory. The power schematic (printed 96) routes YEL / WHT-YEL via 2J9-6/7 to the lower-playfield relay; the separate 2J10-10/9 coin-door branch is outside it. Backbox GI also includes an always-on portion. The before-modification installer photograph contains 35 backbox sockets in three traced portions: 17 upper sockets remain powered, while 6 left and 12 right sockets are relay controlled, so only 18 backbox sockets belong to this output. An independent owner photo's six large-globe #455 blinkers match sockets within those controlled 18 (two left, four right); the other 12 are ordinary lamps. The blinkers operate autonomously while supplied and are not six extra CPU-controlled flashers. Eleven original-stock playfield bayonets belong to lower 16: both three-bank, one left-points, two right-points, one per sling and two per return island. Physical bodies, local wiring, factory routing and 4K lower-only socket depictions reconcile the inventory; renderer collection size is not the count. Quantity 29 includes eleven playfield plus eighteen backbox bulbs. Spatial places only the eleven playfield emitters; the eighteen backbox emitters are cabinet/service locations and need no invented playfield points. Both bank positions use the independent factory measurement; the other nine use actual Bigus bulb meshes checked against 4K and stock wood. Light66 duplicates the sole left-sling bulb, and Light81 incorrectly groups the rear bank bulb as upper. The supplemental Bigus LowerGI member Light67 lies at a round switch-wire passage. A stock native photograph positively shows green and pale leads entering that open bore; its bulb flag does not establish another physical socket. Value 1 on this public address commands GI darkness and 0 commands light in SolLowerGI; this is a relay command, not direct lamp intensity.

Printed Solenoid Table item 23 ("Snd O/L 1"), routed over a ribbon cable to the Sound Overlay Solenoid Board. The manual's own board-local item number (23) is not the PinMAME public address; the offset (public = manual item + 14) is resolved by cross-referencing pinned PinMAME's own doc comment ('37-41 Sound overlay board', core.h) against the retained script's SolCallback registrations. Retained script callback: Sol37, confirming this address directly. The table drives f137/f139/f140 playfield Light effects as well as FlSol backglass proxies. The manual legend defines bp as Back Panel; printed 42 locates D-13356 at the rear of the playfield, and printed 52 lists its #906 flashlamps and #555 GI bulbs. The physical flashers are on that upright rear playfield panel. Renderer backglass proxies are not extra bulbs. The CPU's 1P21 ribbon is shared upstream; the structured control connection identifies the individual board output at SOL J4. The Red Parts Catalog printed 5-37 draws five #906 positions LMP1-LMP5 and five GI positions LMP6-LMP10; the actual original board shows that complete labelled pattern. This settles the physical rear-panel total at five flashers, rather than the operations solenoid table's six. The independent operator's handbook printed 8 explicitly specifies two left, one middle and two right, agreeing with the complete drawing and physical pattern. Each actual socket is projected onto its own front plastic plane: factory/PCB/mount registration supplies X, exact Bigus world-mesh front face supplies Y, with independent header/edge, assembled-board and mounted-stock checks. The projection does not assert actual socket PCB depth or emitter Z; measured X is rounded to three decimals. The operations table's three-left-bulb entry is a quantity erratum; physical quantity 2 follows the corroborated handbook count.
